clips.send: Send this to someone who thinks old-fashioned gender roles just happened naturally - anger at seeing it was manufactured on purpose.
clips.caption:
Look at advertising from a few decades ago and you'll see something that wasn't an accident.

"The chef does everything but cook. That's what wives are for." A real ad, run everywhere, completely normal at the time. He calls it what it actually was: propaganda, coming from agencies, designed on purpose to keep women in a specific role - and he says people close to him in the Brotherhood were involved in exactly that kind of work.

It wasn't persuasion. It was programming, repeated until it looked like culture instead of a campaign.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how to spot the version of this still running today.

clips.send: Send this to someone who thinks old advertising was just corny, not actually dangerous - awe at what they got away with.
clips.caption:
"Boost your personality" was the actual slogan. The personality boost was cocaine.

Early Coca-Cola had cocaine from the coca leaf, caffeine from the cola nut, and sugar - a genuinely physically addictive combination, marketed as a lift for your mood. They knew exactly what they'd put in the bottle.

People trusted the big corporation, trusted the magazine that ran the ad, trusted the government that allowed it. Nobody was lying to themselves. They were being lied to, by people who knew better.
